raw.raw:
[CONDITION_REMOVED:Bloodied Nose]
[COMPANION_CONDITION_REMOVED:Daeris|Unconscious]
[COMPANION_CONDITION_REMOVED:Daeris|Traumatized]
[ARC_COMPLETE:The Glassworks]

The spectral hand drifts out. Crosses the cave floor. Touches the man's shoulder.

He moves.

Slow. Wrong. Like something waking from the bottom of cold water. But he moves.

His head comes up. Eyes open. Focused on nothing for a long moment. Then focused on the hand. Then, with visible effort, on you.

His mouth works.

"How long," he says. Barely voice at all. Cracked lips. Hollow face. The look of a man who stopped counting days some time ago.

He's breathing. Thin. But breathing.

No wounds you can see from here. No blood. Skin the colour of old tallow. Hair grown out past his shoulders. Clothes that were once a working man's kit, now just rags held together by habit.

He's been here a long time.

The terminus stone behind him pulses faintly. Green. Steady. Like a heartbeat that isn't his.

He looks at the stone. Looks back at you.

"It won't let me leave," he says. Flat. Not desperate. He got past desperate a while back. "I've tried. Every tide. It just." He stops. "Puts me back."

Frizwick makes a sound behind you. Very quiet. Not professional at all.

[QUEST_STEP:Aldus Vareth|Determine how to free Aldus from the terminus stone's hold|false]
[QUEST:Aldus Vareth|active]

You move careful. Eyes working the cave first.

The tidal pools catch the green light and throw it in patterns across the ceiling. Nothing moves in them. Nothing underneath the surface that shouldn't be there.

The walls. Natural rock mostly. Some Thassilonian carving where the cave narrows toward the sea entrance. The north face approach Shalelu marked on the sketch. You can see grey daylight through it. Distant. The sound of the ocean.

No goblins. No creatures with wrong joints. Nothing breathing in corners.

The man watches you come. Doesn't flinch. Doesn't reach for anything. No weapon visible. Probably couldn't lift one anyway.

You stop three feet from him.

Close enough now to read the details. Vashari descent, maybe. Dark colouring. The same bone structure as Corven, once you're looking for it. Older than his brother by the look of him. Or just worn harder.

His eyes are clear. That's something. Whatever the terminus stone has been doing to him, it hasn't taken his mind.

He looks at you steadily.

"You're not goblins," he says. Like he's confirming something he'd almost stopped believing possible. "And you're not." He glances at the stone. "One of its."

A pause.

"Someone sent you."

Not a question.

[XP:100]

You crouch beside it.

The stone is chest height. Dense. Older than the Thassilonian carvings on the walls, and those are ten thousand years old. The spiral rune at its centre is worn smooth at the edges from water and tide and time.

Not worn at the middle.

The middle is sharp. Fresh-looking. Like something still uses it.

Green light comes from inside the stone. Not reflected. Generated. Steady pulse, slow and deliberate. The rhythm of something alive, or something built to imitate alive.

Script around the outer ring. Not Thassilonian. Something older. Pre-empire notation, maybe. The kind Daeris would know on sight.

You have a stone disc in your pack. Carved spiral rune. Unknown script.

You pull it out.

Hold it near the terminus stone.

The green light brightens. Just slightly. The pulse quickens. One beat. Then settles back.

Recognition.

Aldus watches you. His jaw tightens.

"Where did you get that," he says. Quiet. Very quiet.

Not asking where you found it.

Asking who gave it to you.

Behind you, Frizwick shifts her weight. She caught it too.

Morwen says nothing. But you can hear her moving closer.

The disc in your hand is warm. It wasn't warm a moment ago.

His face does something complicated.

Starts to close down. Stops. Starts again.

He looks at the disc. Looks at you. The green light catches his eyes and they're wet, suddenly, though he's holding himself very still.

"He's alive," Aldus says.

Not a question either. But different from the last one.

You nod.

He exhales. Long. Shaking at the end. The sound of a man letting go of something he'd been carrying so long he'd forgotten the weight of it.

Then he pulls himself back together. Takes a breath. Another. Sets his jaw the way Corven sets his jaw, the family resemblance landing properly for the first time.

"He sent you here," he says. "To the stone specifically."

You show him the disc. The spiral matches the rune carved into the terminus stone exactly. He looks at it for a long moment.

"He found it," Aldus says. Quiet. Wondering. "I didn't think he'd find it."

He reaches out. Stops himself before touching it. Pulls his hand back.

"It's a key," he says. "Or part of one. I worked that much out." His voice is steadier now. Something to focus on. "I couldn't use it myself. The stone doesn't respond to me anymore."

He meets your eyes.

"It might respond to you."

"I don't know," you say. "Corven gave it to us. Said it was yours. Didn't know what it did."

Aldus goes still.

"He didn't find it," he says slowly. Working through it. "Someone gave it to him."

He looks at the stone. The pulse is still slightly faster than before. Still responding to the disc in your hand.

"I hid it," he says. "Before the stone took me the first time. Left it with a contact in Sandpoint. Someone I trusted." A pause. "Someone who was supposed to get word to Corven directly."

He stops.

"That was a long time ago."

The implication sits there. Someone held onto it. Waited. Passed it along eventually, or passed it to someone who passed it along. A chain of hands between then and now, and you don't know a single name in it.

Morwen speaks from behind you. Careful.

"The contact. Do you have a name?"

Aldus shakes his head. "A location. A drop point. Dockside Sandpoint. Cooper Street."

Frizwick makes a small sound.

Cooper Street. Where Corven lives. Where you met him.

Not a coincidence. Nothing about this has been a coincidence.

Aldus looks at the disc again.

"Someone built this chain deliberately," he says. "And pointed it at me."

He doesn't sound grateful. He sounds afraid.

You press it flat against the spiral rune.

The fit is exact. Edge to edge. Groove to groove. The disc sinks into the stone surface like it was always meant to sit there.

The green light goes white.

Not bright. Absolute. Every shadow in the cave gone for one full second.

Then it dims back. Slower than before. The pulse changes rhythm. Longer between beats. Like something exhaling.

Aldus gasps.

He's on his feet. Didn't stand up. Just, on his feet, stumbling forward, one hand out for balance. You catch his arm without thinking. He grabs it hard.

"I can feel the edge," he says. Urgent. Breathless. "The boundary. I can feel where it ends."

He looks at his feet. The cave floor. The water lapping at the tidal pools.

He takes one step toward the sea entrance.

The stone doesn't pulse.

Another step.

Nothing.

He stops. Turns back. Face stripped of everything careful and contained. Raw. Completely raw.

"It's open," he says.

Morwen is already moving to support him from the other side. Frizwick has the sea entrance covered, blade out, checking the approach without being asked.

The disc is still seated in the stone. Still warm.

You don't know if pulling it out closes the door again.

[QUEST:Aldus Vareth|completed]
[XP:300]

The disc is already there.

Seated flush in the spiral. Still warm under your fingertips where you haven't pulled your hand back yet.

Aldus is standing. Breathing hard. Three steps from the stone and the boundary hasn't snapped shut around him.

Morwen watches the disc. Watches you.

"Leave it," she says quietly. "Until he's clear."

Practical. Right.

The question is what happens when you pull it free. Whether the door closes again behind him. Whether it closes on you. Whether it matters, given the dissolution sequence still waiting upstairs with four blasting charges and a caretaker creature that's been holding this mechanism below threshold since before Thassilon had a name.

Frizwick hasn't looked away from the sea entrance.

Aldus takes another step. Tests the ground with his foot like a man crossing ice he doesn't trust.

Still nothing from the stone.

He looks back at you. At the disc.

"When you take it," he says. Steady. Choosing his words. "Do it fast. And move."

He's thought about this. In the long dark between tides, he's thought about exactly this.

He braces himself.

Waiting on you.

You flick two fingers at her. Move. Now.

She doesn't need more than that. Her arm goes around Aldus, shoulder under his, taking his weight without ceremony. He's heavier than he looks. Or she's stronger than she looks. Either way they move.

Frizwick is already at the sea entrance. Blade put away. Both hands free for climbing or hauling. She scans the north face approach and nods back at you. Clear.

Aldus moves better than expected. Legs remember what his body forgot. Muscle working on instinct while the rest of him runs on pure will.

They're five steps from the entrance.

Ten.

The stone pulses behind you. Longer between beats. Patient. Waiting.

The disc sits warm in its groove. One clean pull and it's done. Or the door closes. Or something else entirely happens that none of you have anticipated because you're working from a ten thousand year old contract read by a woman who spent forty years doing quiet work for someone you haven't found yet.

Morwen gets Aldus to the threshold. Daylight on his face for the first time in however long. He stops there. Just one breath. Eyes closed.

She looks back at you.

Waiting.

Frizwick outside now. Covering the approach.

Your hand is on the disc.

"Stone keeps the door open," he says. Without turning. Eyes still closed. "Permanently."

A beat.

"Or until the tide takes it. I don't know which." He opens his eyes. Looks out at the grey water and the sky. "I never got to test it."

Morwen looks at you. Reading the calculation.

The disc is yours. Corven's, technically. Passed down a chain of careful hands to land here, in this cave, in this exact groove. Leaving it means losing it. Maybe forever. The tide comes in, the stone goes under, and whatever the disc was built to do gets decided by the ocean.

Taking it means the door closes. Maybe the stone resets. Maybe Aldus can't come back through. Maybe that doesn't matter if he's already clear.

Maybe something else was using that boundary as a wall, not a door.

Aldus turns. Looks at you properly. The daylight makes him look worse and better at once. Worse because you can see the full damage. Better because he's standing in it.

"The contract upstairs," he says. "The caretaker. The dissolution sequence." He says it like a man who's been listening through stone for a long time. "Finishing that closes everything. The stone. The channels. All of it."

He meets your eyes.

"You were already planning to."

You take your hand off it.

Walk.

The stone pulses behind you. Steady. Changed rhythm but still present. The green light reaches the cave entrance and stops there, like it knows where its boundary is.

You don't look back.

Five steps. Ten. The rock underfoot shifts from carved Thassilonian precision to raw natural stone. The sound of the ocean gets louder. Salt air. Real air. Grey daylight on your face.

You step through.

Frizwick is two feet to your left. Doesn't say anything. Nods once.

Morwen has Aldus seated on a flat rock above the tideline. He's looking at the water. Not speaking. Just watching it the way a man watches something that held him for a long time and doesn't hold him anymore.

You don't hear the stone close.

You don't hear anything change.

The disc is still down there. Warm in its groove. Holding a door open that nobody else is likely to find.

Morwen looks at you over Aldus's head. One eyebrow up. The question is obvious.

Upstairs. The caretaker. Four charges. The junction stone dense with ten thousand year old script.

Aldus is free. The terminus is open. The only thing left is finishing what the caretaker has been waiting to finish since before Thassilon fell.
